title.zh: 卷八十八 列傳第七十六: 隱逸
title.raw: 卷八十八 列傳第七十六: 隱逸 Volume 88 Biographies 76: Recluses

sentences.zh: 眭誇 馮亮 鄭修 崔廓 子賾 徐則 張文詡

translations.literal: Sui Kua, Feng Liang, Zheng Xiu, Cui Kuo, his son Ze, Xu Ze, Zhang Wensu
translations.idiomatic: Sui Kua, Feng Liang, Zheng Xiu, Cui Kuo and his son Ze, Xu Ze, and Zhang Wensu

sentences.zh: 蓋兼濟獨善，顯晦之殊，其事不同，由來久矣。

translations.literal: For broadly benefiting the world and cultivating goodness alone, the differences between manifesting oneself and withdrawing—their affairs are not the same; this has been so for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Serving the world at large and cultivating virtue in solitude, public engagement and withdrawal from the world—these are different paths, and the distinction is an old one.

sentences.zh: 昔夷、齊獲全于周武，華矞不容于太公，何哉？

translations.literal: In antiquity Boyi and Shuqi were spared by King Wu of Zhou, while Hua Xu found no acceptance from the Grand Duke Jiang—why?
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Boyi and Shuqi were spared by King Wu of Zhou, yet Hua Xu could not abide with the Grand Duke Jiang—what accounts for this?

sentences.zh: 求其心者，許以激貪之用；

translations.literal: Those who seek their inner motives approve of them as a means to stir the greedy to action;
translations.idiomatic: Those who probe their hearts regard them as useful for rousing the greedy;

sentences.zh: 督其跡者，矯以教義之風。

translations.literal: those who scrutinize their deeds correct them with the wind of moral instruction.
translations.idiomatic: those who examine their conduct would reform them with the teaching of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 而肥遁不歸，代有其人矣。

translations.literal: Yet those who grow wealthy in reclusion and never return—each age has had such men.
translations.idiomatic: Yet men who prosper in withdrawal and never return—every generation has known them.

sentences.zh: 故《易》稱「遁世無悶」，「不事王侯」。

translations.literal: Therefore the Changes says, "Withdraw from the world without vexation," and "Do not serve kings and feudal lords."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Classic of Changes speaks of "withdrawal from the world without discontent" and of "not serving kings and feudal lords."

sentences.zh: 《詩》云「皎皎白駒，在彼空谷」。

translations.literal: The Odes says, "Bright, bright the white colt, in that empty valley."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes has it: "Bright, bright the white colt, in that empty valley."

sentences.zh: 《禮》云「儒有上不臣天子，下不事諸侯」。

translations.literal: The Rites says, "The scholar does not serve the Son of Heaven above, nor the feudal lords below."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites states that "the scholar does not serve the Son of Heaven above, nor the feudal lords below."

sentences.zh: 《語》曰「舉逸民，天下之人歸心焉」。

translations.literal: The Analects says, "Raise up reclusive subjects, and all under Heaven will turn their hearts to you."
translations.idiomatic: The Analects teaches that when one "raises up reclusive subjects, all under Heaven will turn their hearts" to the ruler.

sentences.zh: 雖出處殊途，語默異用，各言其志，皆君子之道也。

translations.literal: Though their going forth and staying withdrawn follow different roads, speech and silence have different uses, and each speaks his own purpose—all are the way of the gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Though their paths of engagement and withdrawal differ, and speech and silence serve different ends, each expresses his own intent—all alike belong to the way of the gentleman.

sentences.zh: 洪崖兆其始，箕山扇其風，七人作乎周年，四皓光乎漢日。

translations.literal: Hong Ya opened the way at the beginning; Mount Ji fanned the breeze; the Seven [recluses] arose in the Zhou year; the Four Hoary [Heads] shone in Han days.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Ya marked the beginning; Mount Ji spread the tradition; the Seven [recluses] appeared in the Zhou age; the Four Whiteheads of Mount Shang shone in Han times.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉以降，其流逾廣。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin downward, their stream grew ever wider.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wei and Jin dynasties onward, the current grew ever broader.

sentences.zh: 其大者則輕天下，細萬物；

translations.literal: The great among them lightly esteem All-under-Heaven and look down on ten thousand things;
translations.idiomatic: Those of grand cast disdained the realm and held all things lightly;

sentences.zh: 其小者則安苦節，甘賤貧。

translations.literal: the small among them rest content in harsh integrity and take pleasure in base poverty.
translations.idiomatic: those of lesser stature were content with austere integrity and gladly bore poverty.

sentences.zh: 或與世同塵，隨波瀾以俱逝；

translations.literal: Some mingle their dust with the world and drift away with the billows together;
translations.idiomatic: Some mixed with the world and drifted away with the current;

sentences.zh: 或違時矯俗，望江湖而獨往。

translations.literal: some defy the age and correct custom, gazing toward rivers and lakes as they go alone.
translations.idiomatic: others spurned their times, stood apart from convention, and turned toward rivers and lakes alone.

sentences.zh: 狎玩魚鳥，左右琴書，拾遺粒而織落毛，飲石泉而庇松柏。

translations.literal: They frolic with fish and birds, with zither and books to left and right; they gather fallen grains to weave fallen feathers, drink from stone springs, and shelter under pines and cypresses.
translations.idiomatic: They played with fish and birds, kept zither and books close at hand, gathered stray grains and wove shed feathers, drank from stone springs, and took shelter beneath pines and cypresses.

sentences.zh: 放情宇宙之外，自足懷抱之中。

translations.literal: They release feeling beyond the bounds of the universe and find self-sufficiency within the embrace of the heart.
translations.idiomatic: They let their feelings roam beyond the cosmos and found sufficiency within their own hearts.

sentences.zh: 然皆欣欣於獨善，鮮汲汲於兼濟。

translations.literal: Yet all were glad in solitary goodness, rarely eager for broad benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet all rejoiced in solitary cultivation of virtue and were rarely eager to benefit the world at large.

sentences.zh: 夷情得喪，忘懷累有。

translations.literal: They level feeling in gain and loss and forget cares and accumulations.
translations.idiomatic: They were indifferent to gain and loss and free from burdens of care.

sentences.zh: 比夫邁德弘道，匡俗庇人，可得而小，不可得而忽也。

translations.literal: Compared with those who advance virtue and enlarge the Way, correct custom and shelter the people—they can be regarded as small, but not as negligible.
translations.idiomatic: Beside those who advance virtue, enlarge the Way, correct custom, and shelter the people, they may seem small, yet they cannot be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 而受命哲王，守文令主，莫不束帛交馳，蒲輪結轍，奔走岩穀，唯恐不逮者，何哉？

translations.literal: Yet wise kings who received the Mandate and rulers who guarded the cultural heritage—none failed to send silken bolts in swift exchange and rush carriage wheels in crowded file, hurrying to mountain valleys for fear of not reaching them in time—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet sage kings who received the Mandate and cultured rulers who upheld the tradition—all sent silken gifts in swift succession and rushed wheel-rim carriages in crowded trains to mountain valleys, fearing they might not arrive in time. Why was this?

sentences.zh: 以其道雖未弘，志不可奪，縱無舟楫之功，終有堅貞之操，足以立懦夫之志，息貪競之風。

translations.literal: Because though their Way was not yet broadly displayed, their will could not be wrested away; even if they had no merit of boat and oar, in the end they had steadfast integrity sufficient to establish the will of cowards and quell the wind of greedy rivalry.
translations.idiomatic: Because although their Way had not yet been broadly realized, their resolve could not be broken; even without the achievement of ferrying others across, they possessed steadfast integrity enough to stiffen the spine of the timid and still the wind of greedy rivalry.

sentences.zh: 與苟得之徒，不可同年共日，所謂無用以為用，無為而無不為也。

translations.literal: They cannot be placed in the same year and day as those of grasping gain—the so-called "usefulness in being useless, non-doing by which nothing is left undone."
translations.idiomatic: They cannot be mentioned in the same breath as those who seize what they can—the very sense of "finding use in uselessness, accomplishing all through non-action."

sentences.zh: 自叔世澆浮，淳風殆盡，錐刀之末，競入成群。

translations.literal: From the decadent age when currents grew shallow, pure winds were nearly exhausted; at the tip of an awl, rivalries entered in swarms.
translations.idiomatic: Since the late age when manners grew shallow and pure custom nearly vanished, men scrambled in swarms over the merest trifle.

sentences.zh: 而能冥心物表，介然離俗，望古獨適，求友千齡，亦異人矣！

translations.literal: Yet those who can darken the heart beyond mere things, stand apart and leave the vulgar, look to antiquity in solitary suitability, and seek friends a thousand ages hence—they too are extraordinary men!
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who could still the heart beyond mere things, stand wholly apart from the vulgar world, look to antiquity in solitary accord, and seek companions a thousand years hence—they too were extraordinary men!

sentences.zh: 何必御霞乘雲而追日月，窮極天地，始為超遠哉！

translations.literal: Why must one ride mist and mount clouds chasing sun and moon, exhausting heaven and earth, before counting as surpassingly far!
translations.idiomatic: Why must one ride the clouds and chase the sun and moon, exhausting heaven and earth, before one counts as surpassingly remote!

sentences.zh: 案《魏書》列眭誇、馮亮、李謐、鄭脩為《逸士傳》。

translations.literal: According to the Book of Wei, Sui Kua, Feng Liang, Li Mi, and Zheng Xiu are listed in the "Biographies of Reclusive Gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei records Sui Kua, Feng Liang, Li Mi, and Zheng Xiu in its "Biographies of Reclusive Gentlemen."

sentences.zh: 《隋書》列李士謙、崔廓、廓子賾、徐則、張文詡為《隱逸傳》。

translations.literal: The Book of Sui lists Li Shiqian, Cui Kuo, Kuo's son Ze, Xu Ze, and Zhang Wensu in the "Biographies of Recluses."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Sui places Li Shiqian, Cui Kuo, Kuo's son Ze, Xu Ze, and Zhang Wensu in its "Biographies of Recluses."

sentences.zh: 今以李謐、士謙附其家傳，其餘並編附篇，以備《隱逸傳》云。

translations.literal: Now Li Mi and Shiqian are appended to their family biographies; the rest are all compiled in this fascicle to complete the "Biographies of Recluses."
translations.idiomatic: Here Li Mi and Shiqian are placed in their family biographies; the remainder are gathered in this chapter to complete the "Biographies of Recluses."

sentences.zh: 眭誇，一名旭，趙郡高邑人也。

translations.literal: Sui Kua, also named Xu, was a man of Gaoyi in Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Kua, also called Xu, came from Gaoyi in Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖邁，晉東海王越軍謀掾，後沒石勒，為徐州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mai served as military strategist to Prince Yue of Donghai in Jin; afterward he perished under Shi Le and became Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mai had been military strategist to Prince Yue of Donghai under the Jin, then fell to Shi Le and became Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父邃，字懷道，慕容寶中書令。

translations.literal: His father Sui, styled Huaidao, was Director of the Secretariat under Murong Bao.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sui, styled Huaidao, served Murong Bao as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 誇少有大度，不拘小節，耽好書傳，未曾以世務經心。

translations.literal: Kua in youth had great breadth of spirit, not bound by petty matters; he loved books and records fondly and never once took worldly affairs to heart.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Kua had a generous spirit and cared nothing for petty constraints; devoted to books and records, he never let worldly business weigh on his mind.

sentences.zh: 好飲酒，浩然物表。

translations.literal: He loved drinking wine and was vast and detached beyond mere things.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine and lived with an expansive detachment beyond the world of affairs.

sentences.zh: 年三十，遭父喪，須鬢致白，每一悲哭，聞者為之流涕。

translations.literal: At age thirty he suffered his father's death; his beard and temples turned white; each time he wept in grief, those who heard him shed tears for him.
translations.idiomatic: At thirty he lost his father; his beard and temples turned white, and each time he wept in mourning those who heard him wept as well.

sentences.zh: 高尚不仕，寄情丘壑。

translations.literal: Lofty and aloof, he would not serve; he entrusted his feelings to hills and ravines.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty in character, he would not take office and entrusted his heart to hills and valleys.

sentences.zh: 同郡李順願與之交，誇拒而不許。

translations.literal: Li Shun of the same commandery wished to befriend him; Kua refused and would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shun of the same commandery wished to befriend him, but Kua refused.

sentences.zh: 邦國少長莫不憚之。

translations.literal: Young and old throughout the state all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Young and old throughout the region all stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 少與崔浩為莫逆之交。

translations.literal: In youth he was sworn friends with Cui Hao.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was sworn friends with Cui Hao.

sentences.zh: 浩為司徒，奏徵為中郎，辭疾不赴。

translations.literal: When Hao became Grand Tutor, he memorialized to summon Kua as Gentleman-in-Attendance; Kua pleaded illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao became Grand Tutor, he memorialized to summon Kua as Gentleman-in-Attendance, but Kua pleaded illness and declined.

sentences.zh: 州郡逼遣，不得已，入京都，與浩相見。

translations.literal: The province and commandery pressed and sent him off; having no choice, he entered the capital and met with Hao.
translations.idiomatic: The province and commandery pressed him until he had no choice but to enter the capital and see Hao.

sentences.zh: 經留數日，唯飲酒談敘平生，不及世利。

translations.literal: He stayed several days, only drinking wine and discussing their lives together, not touching on worldly profit.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed several days, drinking wine and talking over their lives together, never touching worldly gain.

sentences.zh: 浩每欲論屈之，竟不能發言，其見敬憚如此。

translations.literal: Each time Hao wished to argue and bend him, he ultimately could not speak; such was the respect and awe in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Hao wished to argue and win him over, he could not bring himself to speak—such was the respect and awe Kua inspired.

sentences.zh: 浩後遂投詔書於誇懷，亦不開口。

translations.literal: Later Hao tossed an imperial edict into Kua's bosom; he still did not open his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Later Hao tossed an imperial edict into Kua's bosom, but Kua still would not speak.

sentences.zh: 誇曰：「桃簡，卿已為司徒，何足以此勞國士也？

translations.literal: Kua said, "Taojian, you are already Grand Tutor—why trouble a man of the state with this?
translations.idiomatic: Kua said, "Taojian, you are already Grand Tutor—why bother a man of the realm with such a thing?

sentences.zh: 吾便將別。

translations.literal: I am about to take my leave."
translations.idiomatic: I shall take my leave now."

sentences.zh: 」桃簡，浩小名。

translations.literal: " Taojian was Hao's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: " Taojian was Hao's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 浩慮誇即還，時乘一騾，更無兼騎，乃以誇騾內之廄中，冀相維縶。

translations.literal: Hao, fearing Kua would return at once—at the time he rode a single mule with no spare mount—put Kua's mule inside the stable, hoping thereby to detain him.
translations.idiomatic: Hao, fearing Kua would leave at once—for he himself rode a single mule with no spare mount—stabled Kua's mule in his own stable, hoping to detain him.

sentences.zh: 誇遂托鄉人輸租者，謬為御車，乃得出關。

translations.literal: Kua then entrusted himself to a fellow townsman who delivered rent grain, falsely claiming him as carriage driver, and thus got out through the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Kua then joined a fellow townsman delivering rent grain, passed himself off as the driver's assistant, and thus got through the pass.

sentences.zh: 浩知而歎曰：「眭誇獨行士，本不應以小職辱之，又使其人杖策復路，吾當何辭以謝也！

translations.literal: When Hao learned of it he sighed: "Sui Kua is a man who walks alone; he ought not to have been insulted with a petty office, and to make him staff in hand return on the road—what words can I offer in apology!
translations.idiomatic: When Hao learned of it he sighed, "Sui Kua is a man who walks his own path; he should never have been insulted with a petty post, and to send him staff in hand back along the road—what words can I offer in apology?

sentences.zh: 」時朝法甚峻，誇既私還，將有私歸之咎。

translations.literal: " At the time court law was very strict; since Kua had returned privately, he would have been charged with unauthorized departure.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time court law was severe; since Kua had returned without permission, he faced punishment for unauthorized departure.

sentences.zh: 浩仍相左右，始得無坐。

translations.literal: Hao still aided him on either side, and only then did he escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Hao still shielded him on both sides, and only then did Kua escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 經年，送誇本騾，兼遺以所乘馬，為書謝之。

translations.literal: After more than a year he sent Kua his original mule, together with the gift of the horse he himself had ridden, with a letter of apology.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he sent Kua his original mule along with the horse he himself had ridden, with a letter of apology.

sentences.zh: 誇更不受其騾馬，亦不復書。

translations.literal: Kua in turn would not accept the mule or horse, nor would he write back.
translations.idiomatic: Kua would not accept the mule or horse and wrote no reply.

sentences.zh: 及浩沒，為之素服，受鄉人弔唁，經一時乃止。

translations.literal: When Hao died, Kua wore unbleached mourning for him and accepted condolences from fellow townsfolk; after a season he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao died, Kua wore plain mourning for him and accepted condolences from fellow townsfolk; after a season he ceased.

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「崔公既死，誰能更容眭誇！

translations.literal: He sighed: "Now that Lord Cui is dead, who can still tolerate Sui Kua!
translations.idiomatic: He sighed, "Now that Lord Cui is dead, who can still tolerate Sui Kua?

sentences.zh: 」婦父巨鹿魏攀，當時名達之士，未嘗備婿之禮，情同朋好。

translations.literal: " His father-in-law Wei Pan of Julu was a man of renown in his day; he never once performed the ritual due a son-in-law, yet their feelings were like those between friends.
translations.idiomatic: " His father-in-law Wei Pan of Julu was a celebrated man of the day; he never observed the formal rites due a son-in-law, yet they were friends in spirit.

sentences.zh: 或人謂誇曰：「吾聞有大才者必居貴仕，子何獨在桑榆乎？

translations.literal: Someone said to Kua: "I hear that men of great talent are sure to hold noble office—why do you alone remain in the evening of your years?
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Kua, "I hear that men of great talent always hold high office—why do you alone linger in life's twilight?

sentences.zh: 」遂著《知命論》以釋之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he wrote "On Knowing Fate" to explain.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he wrote "On Knowing Fate" to explain himself.

sentences.zh: 及卒，葬日赴會者如市。

translations.literal: At his death, those who came to the funeral were like a market.
translations.idiomatic: At his death, mourners at the funeral filled the streets like a market fair.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: He left no sons.

sentences.zh: 馮亮，字靈通，南陽人，梁平北將軍蔡道恭之甥也。

translations.literal: Feng Liang, styled Lingtong, was a man of Nanyang, nephew to Cai Daogong, General Who Pacifies the North for Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Liang, styled Lingtong, came from Nanyang and was nephew to Cai Daogong, Liang's General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 少博覽諸書，又篤好佛理。

translations.literal: In youth he broadly perused all books and was also deeply devoted to Buddhist principles.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he read widely and was deeply devoted to Buddhist teaching.

sentences.zh: 隨道恭至義陽，會中山王英平義陽，獲焉。

translations.literal: He followed Daogong to Yiyang; when Prince of Zhongshan Ying pacified Yiyang, he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Daogong to Yiyang; when Prince Ying of Zhongshan pacified Yiyang, Liang was taken captive.

sentences.zh: 英素聞其名，以禮待接。

translations.literal: Ying had long heard his name and received him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Ying had long known his reputation and treated him with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 亮性清靜，後隱居嵩山，感英之德，以時展覲。

translations.literal: Liang by nature was pure and still; afterward he lived in reclusion on Mount Song, moved by Ying's virtue, and from time to time paid his respects.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was by nature serene; later he lived in seclusion on Mount Song, grateful for Ying's kindness, and visited him from time to time.

sentences.zh: 英亡，亮奔赴，盡其哀慟。

translations.literal: When Ying died, Liang hurried to the scene and expressed his grief and anguish to the full.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying died, Liang hastened to mourn him and grieved to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 宣武嘗召以為羽林監，領中書舍人，將令侍講《十地》諸經，固辭不許。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu once summoned him to be Supervisor of the Feathered Forest and concurrently Palace Gentleman of the Secretariat, intending to have him attend and lecture on the Dasabhumi and other sutras; he firmly declined and would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu once summoned him as Supervisor of the Feathered Forest and concurrent Palace Gentleman of the Secretariat, intending to have him lecture on the Dasabhumi and other sutras, but Liang firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 又欲使衣幘入見，苦求以幅巾就朝，遂不強逼。

translations.literal: They also wished to have him wear the formal cap to enter audience; he earnestly begged to attend court in a plain headcloth, and they did not force him.
translations.idiomatic: They also wished him to wear formal court dress for audience, but he earnestly begged to attend in a plain headcloth, and they did not press him.

sentences.zh: 還山數年，與僧禮誦為業，蔬食飲水，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: He returned to the mountain for several years, taking ritual chanting with monks as his occupation, eating vegetables and drinking water, with the will to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the mountain for several years, devoting himself to chanting with monks, eating only vegetables and drinking water, resolved to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 會逆人王敞事發，連山中沙門法。

translations.literal: When the affair of the rebel Wang Chang broke out, it implicated the monks of the mountain in the law.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Wang Chang's plot was exposed, the mountain monks were implicated as well.

sentences.zh: 而亮被執赴尚書省，十餘日，詔特免雪。

translations.literal: Liang was seized and taken to the Ministry of the Interior; after more than ten days an edict especially exempted and cleared him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was seized and taken to the Ministry of the Interior; after more than ten days an edict specially cleared him.

sentences.zh: 亮不敢還山，遂寓居景明寺，敕給衣食及其從者數人。

translations.literal: Liang dared not return to the mountain and therefore lodged at Jingming Temple; an edict supplied food and clothing for him and several followers.
translations.idiomatic: Liang dared not return to the mountain and lodged at Jingming Temple; an edict provided food and clothing for him and several attendants.

sentences.zh: 後思其舊居，復還山室。

translations.literal: Later, thinking of his old dwelling, he returned once more to his mountain chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Later, longing for his old home, he returned to his mountain dwelling.

sentences.zh: 亮既雅愛山水，又兼工思，結架岩林，甚得棲遊之適。

translations.literal: Liang both loved landscape by nature and was also skilled in design; he built structures among cliffs and forests and found great suitability for dwelling and roaming.
translations.idiomatic: Liang loved landscape by nature and was skilled in design; he built among cliffs and forests and found there the perfect place to live and wander.

sentences.zh: 頗以此聞，宣武給其工力，令與沙門統僧暹、河南尹甄深等同視嵩山形勝之處，遂造閒居佛寺。

translations.literal: This became widely known; Xuanwu supplied him laborers and ordered him together with the Supervisor of Monks Sengxian and Intendant of Henan Zhen Shen and others jointly to survey the scenic places of Mount Song, whereupon they built the Secluded Dwelling Buddhist Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Word of this spread; Xuanwu supplied laborers and ordered him, together with the Supervisor of Monks Sengxian, Intendant of Henan Zhen Shen, and others, to survey Mount Song's finest sites, where they built the Secluded Dwelling Buddhist Temple.

sentences.zh: 林泉既奇，營制又美，曲盡山居之妙。

translations.literal: The woods and springs were already marvelous, and the construction was also beautiful, fully expressing the wonders of mountain dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: The woods and springs were sublime, the construction exquisite—together they captured every charm of life in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 亮時出京師。

translations.literal: Liang would at times come out to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Liang would sometimes visit the capital.

sentences.zh: 延昌二年冬，因遇篤疾，宣武敕以馬輿送令還山，居嵩高道場寺，數日卒。

translations.literal: In winter of the second year of Yanchang, he fell gravely ill; Xuanwu ordered him sent back to the mountain in a horse litter; he dwelt at Songgao Daochang Temple and died within several days.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of the second year of Yanchang he fell gravely ill; Xuanwu ordered him carried back to the mountain in a horse litter; he stayed at Songgao Daochang Temple and died within days.

sentences.zh: 詔贈帛二百匹，以供凶事。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed two hundred bolts of silk to supply funeral expenses.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted two hundred bolts of silk for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 遺誡兄子綜，殮以衣蒨，左手持板，右手執《孝經》一卷，置屍磐石上，去人數里外，積十餘日，乃焚於山，灰燼處，起佛塔經藏。

translations.literal: He left instructions to his nephew Zong: enshroud him in plain hemp garments; in his left hand hold a tablet, in his right hand hold one scroll of the Classic of Filial Piety; place the corpse on a boulder several li from people; after more than ten days burn him on the mountain; at the place of ashes erect a pagoda and sutra repository.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed his nephew Zong to enshroud him in plain hemp, place a tablet in his left hand and a scroll of the Classic of Filial Piety in his right, lay his body on a boulder several li from any dwelling, wait more than ten days, then burn him on the mountain; at the site of the ashes a pagoda and sutra repository were raised.

sentences.zh: 初、亮以盛冬喪，連日驟雪，窮山荒澗，鳥獸饑窘，僵屍山野，無所防護。

translations.literal: At first, since Liang died in deep winter and snow fell in sudden bursts for days on end, in remote mountains and desolate ravines birds and beasts were starving and distressed; a stiff corpse lay in the wild hills with nothing to protect it.
translations.idiomatic: At first, since Liang died in deep winter and snow fell day after day, in remote mountains and desolate ravines birds and beasts were starving; his stiff corpse lay in the wild hills, wholly unprotected.

sentences.zh: 時有壽春道人惠需，每旦往看其屍，拂去塵霰。

translations.literal: At the time the Shouyang monk Huixu each morning went to look at the corpse and brushed away dust and snow.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the monk Huixu of Shouyang went each morning to view the corpse and brush away dust and snow.

sentences.zh: 禽蟲之跡，交橫左右，而初無侵毀。

translations.literal: The tracks of birds and insects crisscrossed to left and right, yet at first there was no violation or harm.
translations.idiomatic: The tracks of birds and insects crisscrossed all around, yet nothing had harmed the body.

sentences.zh: 衣服如本，唯風蒨巾。

translations.literal: His clothes were as before, only the hemp headcloth had been blown by the wind.
translations.idiomatic: His clothes were unchanged; only the hemp headcloth had been stirred by the wind.

sentences.zh: 又以亮識舊南方法師信大栗十枚，言期之將來十地果報，開亮手，以置把中。

translations.literal: Moreover, because Liang had known the southern monk Xin, he placed ten large chestnuts in his hand, saying he expected in the future the fruit of the ten stages; he opened Liang's hand and set them in his grasp.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, because Liang had known the southern monk Xin, he placed ten large chestnuts in his hand, saying he awaited the future reward of the ten bodhisattva stages; he opened Liang's hand and laid them in his palm.

sentences.zh: 經宿，乃為蟲鳥盜食，皮殼在地，而亦不傷肌體。

translations.literal: After a night they were stolen and eaten by insects and birds; the shells lay on the ground, yet the flesh was not harmed.
translations.idiomatic: After a night insects and birds had eaten them; the shells lay on the ground, yet his flesh was unharmed.

sentences.zh: 焚燎之日，有素霧蓊鬱，回繞其傍，自地屬天，彌朝不絕。

translations.literal: On the day of burning, a white mist rose thick and lush, circling about him from earth to heaven, lasting the whole morning without cease.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the cremation, a white mist rose thick about him, circling from earth to heaven and lasting the whole morning.

sentences.zh: 山中道俗營助者百餘人，莫不異焉。

translations.literal: More than a hundred lay and monastic helpers on the mountain who attended the rites—all marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred lay and monastic helpers on the mountain who attended the rites—all were astonished.

sentences.zh: 鄭修，北海人也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xiu was a man of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xiu came from Beihai.

sentences.zh: 少隱于岐南凡穀中，依岩結宇，不交世俗，雅好經史，專意玄門。

translations.literal: In youth he lived in reclusion in Fangu Valley south of Qi, building a dwelling against the cliffs, not mingling with the vulgar world; he loved the classics and histories by nature and devoted himself to the arcane gate.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he lived in seclusion in Fangu Valley south of Qi, building his dwelling against the cliffs, shunning worldly contact; he loved the classics and histories and devoted himself to the arcane teachings.

sentences.zh: 前後州將，每徵不至。

translations.literal: Successive provincial governors summoned him, but each time he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Successive provincial governors summoned him, but he never came.

sentences.zh: 岐州刺史魏蘭根頻遣致命，修不得已，暫出見蘭根，尋還山舍。

translations.literal: Wei Langen, Inspector of Qi, repeatedly sent urgent summons; Xiu had no choice, briefly came out to see Langen, and soon returned to his mountain dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Langen, Inspector of Qi, sent repeated urgent summons; Xiu had no choice but to emerge briefly to see him, then soon returned to his mountain dwelling.

sentences.zh: 蘭根申表薦修，明帝詔付雍州刺史蕭寶夤訪實以聞。

translations.literal: Langen submitted a memorial recommending Xiu; Emperor Ming ordered that it be entrusted to Xiao Baoyin, Inspector of Yong, to investigate the facts and report.
translations.idiomatic: Langen memorialized recommending Xiu; Emperor Ming ordered Xiao Baoyin, Inspector of Yong, to investigate and report.

sentences.zh: 會寶夤作逆，事不行。

translations.literal: When Baoyin rebelled, the matter came to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: But when Baoyin rebelled, the matter came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 崔廓，字士玄，博陵安平人也。

translations.literal: Cui Kuo, styled Shixuan, was a man of Anping in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Kuo, styled Shixuan, came from Anping in Boling commandery.

sentences.zh: 父子元，齊燕州司馬。

translations.literal: His father Ziyuan was Administrator of Yan province under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ziyuan had been Administrator of Yan province under the Qi.

sentences.zh: 廓少孤貧，母賤，由是不為邦族所齒。

translations.literal: Kuo in youth was orphaned and poor; his mother was of low status, and for this reason the clan did not rank him among them.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo lost his father early and grew up poor; his mother was of humble birth, and for this the clan looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 初為裏佐，屢逢屈辱，於是感激，逃入山中。

translations.literal: At first he served as village aide, repeatedly suffered humiliation, and so stirred by emotion fled into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as a village aide and was repeatedly humiliated; stirred by this, he fled into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 遂博覽書籍，多所通涉，山東學者皆宗之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he broadly read books, had wide mastery in many fields, and scholars east of the mountains all took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: He then read widely across many books and gained broad mastery; scholars throughout the eastern provinces all looked to him as their leader.

sentences.zh: 既還鄉，不應辟命。

translations.literal: When he had returned to his native place, he did not respond to summons to office.
translations.idiomatic: After he returned home, he declined all summons to office.

sentences.zh: 與趙郡李士謙為忘言友，時稱崔、李。

translations.literal: With Li Shiqian of Zhao commandery he was a friend who needed no words; the age called them Cui and Li.
translations.idiomatic: He and Li Shiqian of Zhao commandery were friends who needed no words between them; their day knew them simply as Cui and Li.

sentences.zh: 士謙死，廓哭之慟，為之作傳，輸之秘府。

translations.literal: When Shiqian died, Kuo mourned him deeply, wrote a biography for him, and submitted it to the secret archives.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiqian died, Kuo wept for him with deep grief, wrote his biography, and deposited it in the imperial archives.

sentences.zh: 士謙妻盧氏寡居，每家事，輒令人諮廓取定。

translations.literal: Shiqian's wife, Lady Lu, lived as a widow; whenever a household matter arose, she would have someone consult Kuo to decide it.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian's widow, Lady Lu, would send someone to consult Kuo on every household matter before deciding.

sentences.zh: 廓嘗著論言刑名之理，其義甚精，文多不載。

translations.literal: Kuo once composed a treatise on the principles of law and punishment; its meaning was very refined, but most of the text is not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo once wrote a treatise on legal principles that was remarkably subtle; most of it is not reproduced here.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，終於家。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of Sui, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui Daye era, he died at home.

sentences.zh: 子賾，字祖浚，七歲能屬文。

translations.literal: His son Ze, styled Zujun, at age seven could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ze, styled Zujun, could compose prose by the age of seven.

sentences.zh: 容貌短小，有口辯。

translations.literal: His appearance was short in stature, and he had eloquence in speech.
translations.idiomatic: He was short in stature but gifted with eloquence.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，秦孝王薦之，射策高第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Prince Xiao of Qin recommended him, and in the policy examination he ranked at the top.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang reign, Prince Xiao of Qin recommended him; he took top honors in the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 詔與諸儒定樂，授校書郎，轉協律郎。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to work with the Confucian scholars to fix the music; he was appointed Collator, then transferred to Music Harmonizer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to work with the Confucian scholars on fixing the court music; he was appointed Collator and later promoted to Music Harmonizer.

sentences.zh: 太常卿蘇威雅重之。

translations.literal: Su Wei, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, held him in deep regard.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職，性至孝，水漿不入口者五日。

translations.literal: On his mother's bereavement he left office; by nature utterly filial, for five days he took in neither water nor food.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother; utterly filial by nature, he took neither food nor water for five days.

sentences.zh: 後徵為河南、豫章二王侍讀，每更日來往二王之第。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned as Reader to the two princes of Henan and Yuzhang, each day alternating between the two princes' residences.
translations.idiomatic: He was later summoned as Reader to the Princes of Henan and Yuzhang, shuttling between their residences day by day.

sentences.zh: 及河南為晉王，轉記室參軍，自此去豫章。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Henan became Prince of Jin, he was transferred to Staff Recorder, and from this time left Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Henan became Prince of Jin, Ze was made Staff Recorder and ceased attending the Prince of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 王重之不已，遺賾書曰：

translations.literal: The prince valued him without cease and sent Ze a letter, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The prince cherished him ever more highly and sent Ze a letter saying:

sentences.zh: 昔漢氏西京，梁王建國，平臺東苑，慕義如林，馬卿辭武騎之官，枚乘罷弘農之守。

translations.literal: In former times the Han had their Western Capital, Liang Wang established his state, the level terrace and eastern park drew aspirants thick as a forest; Ma Qing resigned his Martial Cavalry post, Mei Sheng relinquished his Hongnong governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In the Western Han capital and in the realm of Prince Xiao of Liang, terraces and eastern parks drew men seeking patronage in throngs; Sima Xiangru gave up his Martial Cavalry post, and Mei Sheng resigned his Hongnong governorship.

sentences.zh: 每覽史傳，嘗竊怪之：何乃脫略官榮，棲遲籓邸？

translations.literal: Each time I read the histories I have privately wondered: why did they cast off official glory and linger at a prince's residence?
translations.idiomatic: Reading the histories, I have often wondered privately: why did they spurn official honors and linger at a prince's mansion?

sentences.zh: 以今望古，方知雅志。

translations.literal: Viewing the ancients from today, I now understand their refined intent.
translations.idiomatic: Only by comparing past and present do I grasp their lofty purpose.

sentences.zh: 彼二子者，豈徒然哉！

translations.literal: Those two men—were they mere idlers!
translations.idiomatic: Those two were no mere idlers!

sentences.zh: 足下博聞強記，鉤深致遠，視漢臣之三篋，似陟蒙山；

translations.literal: You, sir, are broadly learned and strongly retentive, probing deep and reaching far; to view the Han minister's three satchels seems like climbing Mount Meng;
translations.idiomatic: You are widely learned and deeply retentive, probing the profound and reaching far; beside the Han minister's three satchels of books, you seem to climb Mount Meng;

sentences.zh: 對梁相之五車，若吞雲夢。

translations.literal: Facing the Liang chancellor's five cartloads, it is as if swallowing Lake Yunmeng.
translations.idiomatic: and facing the Liang chancellor's five cartloads of books, you seem to swallow Lake Yunmeng whole.

sentences.zh: 吾兄欽賢重士，敬愛忘疲，先築郭隗之宮，常置穆生之醴。

translations.literal: My elder brother honors the worthy and esteems scholars, esteeming and loving them without tiring; he first built a palace like Guo Kui's, and constantly set out wine like for Mu Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: My elder brother reveres worthies and esteems scholars, honoring them without growing weary; he has built a hall in the manner of Guo Kui and keeps wine ready as for Mu Sheng.

sentences.zh: 今者重開土宇，更誓山河。

translations.literal: Now our territory is newly opened and our oaths of lordship renewed.
translations.idiomatic: Our realm has been enlarged afresh and our bond with the land renewed.

sentences.zh: 地方七百，牢籠曲阜；

translations.literal: Our territory spans seven hundred li, encompassing Qufu;
translations.idiomatic: Our domain spans seven hundred li, embracing all that Qufu represents;

sentences.zh: 城兼七十，包舉臨淄。

translations.literal: Our cities number seventy combined, embracing Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: our cities number seventy and more, taking in all that Linzi once held.

sentences.zh: 大啟南陽，方開東閤。

translations.literal: We broadly open our southern capital and are just now opening the eastern pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: We have opened wide the southern residence and are preparing the eastern pavilion for guests.

sentences.zh: 想得奉飛蓋，曳長裾，藉玳筵，躡珠履，歌山桂之偃蹇，賦池竹之檀欒。

translations.literal: I imagine you will ride beneath flying carriage canopies, trail long robes, sit on mother-of-pearl mats, step in pearl-studded slippers, sing of the mountain cassia's towering grace, and compose verses on the pool bamboo's luxuriant clumps.
translations.idiomatic: I imagine you riding beneath the carriage canopy, trailing your long robe, seated on inlaid mats, shod in pearl-studded slippers, singing of the cassias on the hill and composing verses on the bamboos by the pool.

sentences.zh: 其崇貴也如彼，其風流也如此，幸甚幸甚，何樂如之！

translations.literal: Your honored standing will be as exalted as that, your elegance as graceful as this—doubly fortunate, doubly fortunate; what joy could equal it!
translations.idiomatic: To rise so high in honor and grace—to live with such elegance—what greater fortune could there be!

sentences.zh: 高視上京，有懷德祖；

translations.literal: Gazing toward the upper capital, I cherish memory of Dezu;
translations.idiomatic: Looking toward the imperial capital, I think of Yang Xiu;

sentences.zh: 才謝天人，多慚子建。

translations.literal: My talent falls short of heaven and man, and I am much ashamed before Zijian.
translations.idiomatic: My talent falls far short of his, and I feel much ashamed before Cao Zhi.

sentences.zh: 書不盡意，寧俟繁辭。

translations.literal: The letter cannot exhaust my meaning; how could I wait for lengthy phrasing.
translations.idiomatic: Words cannot exhaust what I feel; I will not weary you with more.

sentences.zh: 賾答曰：

translations.literal: Ze replied:
translations.idiomatic: Ze replied:

sentences.zh: 一昨伏奉教書，榮貺非恆，心靈自失。

translations.literal: Yesterday I humbly received your instructive letter; the honor bestowed was beyond the ordinary, and my spirit was quite lost.
translations.idiomatic: Only yesterday I received your gracious letter; the honor you showed me was beyond ordinary measure, and I was quite overwhelmed.

sentences.zh: 若乃理高《象系》，管輅思而不解；

translations.literal: As for reasoning that surpasses the Image and Attached texts, Guan Lu would ponder yet not understand;
translations.idiomatic: Reasoning higher than the Image and Attached texts of the Changes—Guan Lu would ponder it and fail to understand;

sentences.zh: 事富《山海》，郭璞注而未詳。

translations.literal: Matters richer than the Mountains and Seas, Guo Pu would annotate yet not exhaust.
translations.idiomatic: Learning richer than the Classic of Mountains and Seas—Guo Pu would annotate it and still not exhaust it.

sentences.zh: 至於五色相宣，八音繁會，鳳鳴不足喻，龍章莫之比。

translations.literal: As for the five colors blending in harmony, the eight tones gathering in profusion—phoenix song is insufficient as simile, dragon markings have none to compare.
translations.idiomatic: As for harmonies of color and sound woven together—phoenix song is too slight a metaphor, dragon markings too poor a comparison.

sentences.zh: 吳劄之論《周頌》，詎盡揄揚；

translations.literal: Wu Zha's discourse on the Zhou hymns—how could it fully extol?
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zha's praise of the Zhou hymns could scarcely do justice;

sentences.zh: 郢客之奏《陽春》，誰能赴節？

translations.literal: The Ying guest's performance of "Spring in Yang"—who could match its measure?
translations.idiomatic: and when a visitor from Ying played "Spring in Yang," who could keep the measure?

sentences.zh: 伏惟令王殿下，稟潤天潢，承輝日觀，雅道邁于東平，文藝高於北海。

translations.literal: Humbly considering Your Illustrious Highness the prince: you received the moisture of the Heavenly Ford, inherit radiance from Ri'guan, your refined way surpasses the Prince of Dongping, your literary arts exceed the Prince of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness draws your grace from the imperial line and your radiance from the eastern peak; in refined conduct you surpass the Prince of Dongping, in literary art you exceed the Prince of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 漢則馬遷、蕭望，晉則裴楷、張華。

translations.literal: In Han there were Sima Qian and Xiao Wang; in Jin there were Pei Kai and Zhang Hua.
translations.idiomatic: The Han had Sima Qian and Xiao Wangzhi; the Jin had Pei Kai and Zhang Hua.

sentences.zh: 雞樹騰聲，鵷池播美，望我清塵，悠然路絕。

translations.literal: At the Phoenix Tree voices rise, at the Luan Pool beauty spreads; gazing at my slight dust, the way between us yawns impossibly far.
translations.idiomatic: Your fame resounds in the court grove and spreads beside the imperial pool; gazing up at your brilliance, I find the path between us impossibly far.

sentences.zh: 祖浚燕南贅客，河朔惰游，本無意于希顏，豈有心于慕藺。

translations.literal: Zujun is a superfluous guest south of Yan, an idle wanderer north of the River, by nature without intent to emulate Yan Hui, how could he have mind to admire Lin Xiangru?
translations.idiomatic: I am but a stray guest from south of Yan, an idler drifting through the north—never minded to emulate Yan Hui, never dreamed of rivaling Lin Xiangru.

sentences.zh: 未嘗聚螢映雪，懸頭刺股。

translations.literal: I have never gathered fireflies to read by or studied in snow-reflected light, hung my hair from a beam or stabbed my thigh.
translations.idiomatic: I never burned fireflies to read by winter light or stuck needles in my thigh to stay awake.

sentences.zh: 讀《論》唯取一篇，披《莊》不過盈尺。

translations.literal: Reading the Analects I take only one section; opening Zhuangzi I proceed no more than a foot.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Analects I know but one chapter; of Zhuangzi I have read barely a scroll's length.

sentences.zh: 況復桑榆漸暮，藜藿屢空，舉燭無成，穿楊盡棄。

translations.literal: Moreover sunset approaches the mulberry and elm, wild greens are often empty, lifting candles achieves nothing, shooting willow leaves all abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: My years advance like the sun toward the mulberry trees; my pantry stands empty; I cannot light a candle to any purpose, nor hit the willow leaf with my bow.

sentences.zh: 但以燕求馬首，薛養雞鳴，謬齒鴻儀，虛班驥ＩＺ。

translations.literal: Yet only because Yan sought the horse's head and Xue fostered the rooster's crow, I wrongly take rank among the great ceremony and falsely hold place in the fine horses' roster (驥尾).
translations.idiomatic: Yet as Yan sought the steed's head and Xue kept the cock to greet the dawn, I have wrongly been counted among your grand retainers and given a place on the roster of fine steeds.

sentences.zh: 挾太山而超海，比報德而非難；

translations.literal: To embrace Mount Tai and leap over the sea—compared with repaying gratitude this is not difficult;
translations.idiomatic: To shoulder Mount Tai and cross the sea would be easier than repaying your kindness;

sentences.zh: 堙昆侖以為池，匹酬恩而反易。

translations.literal: To dam Kunlun to make a pool—matched with fulfilling gratitude, on the contrary it is easy.
translations.idiomatic: yet damming Kunlun to make a pond would prove harder than rewarding your grace—mine is the easy part.

sentences.zh: 忽屬周桐錫瑞，唐水承家，門有將相，樹宜桃李。

translations.literal: Suddenly it falls to Zhou's parasol-tree receiving auspicious portents, Tang's waters inheriting the family—at the gate are generals and ministers, on the tree peach and plum should flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly Heaven has blessed the Zhou parasol-tree and the Tang waters flow to your house; generals and ministers grace your gate, and peach and plum should flourish on your line.

sentences.zh: 真龍將下，誰好有名；

translations.literal: The true dragon is about to descend—who would delight in mere reputation?
translations.idiomatic: The true dragon is about to descend—who would cling to empty fame?

sentences.zh: 濫吹先逃，何須別聽。

translations.literal: The impostor flute-player flees first; why need another audition?
translations.idiomatic: The impostor in the orchestra would flee first—why should you seek another musician?

sentences.zh: 但慈旨抑揚，損上益下，江海所以稱王，丘陵為之不逮。

translations.literal: Only your kind instruction modulates tone, diminishing the superior to benefit the inferior—thereby rivers and seas are called kings, and hills and mounds cannot match them.
translations.idiomatic: Only your gracious words, raising the low and tempering the high, make rivers and seas king over hills that cannot rival them.

sentences.zh: 曹植儻豫聞高論，則不殞令名；

translations.literal: If Cao Zhi perchance heard your lofty discourse, he would not lose his fine reputation;
translations.idiomatic: Had Cao Zhi heard your lofty discourse, his fair name would not have perished;

sentences.zh: 楊脩若竊在下風，亦詎虧淳德。

translations.literal: If Yang Xiu secretly stood leeward below, would he still diminish his pure virtue?
translations.idiomatic: and had Yang Xiu stood in your lee, his pure virtue would not have suffered.

sentences.zh: 無任荷戴之至，謹奉啟以聞。

translations.literal: I cannot bear the utmost of burden and support; respectfully I offer this report to inform you.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot express how deeply I am obliged; I respectfully submit this in reply.

sentences.zh: 大業四年，從駕汾陽宮，次河陽鎮。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daye, he followed the imperial procession to Fenyang Palace, stopping at Heyang garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daye, he accompanied the emperor to Fenyang Palace and halted at Heyang Station.

sentences.zh: 藍田令王曇于藍田山得一玉人，長三四寸，著大領衣，冠幘。

translations.literal: Wang Tan, Magistrate of Lantian, at Mount Lantian obtained a jade figure three or four inches tall, wearing great-collared robes and a headcloth with narrow turban.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tan, Magistrate of Lantian, found in Mount Lantian a jade figure three or four inches tall, dressed in broad-collared robes and wearing a cap with turban.

sentences.zh: 奏之。

translations.literal: He presented a memorial on it.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the court about it.

sentences.zh: 詔問群臣，莫有識者。

translations.literal: An edict asked the ministers; none recognized it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned his ministers, but none could identify it.

sentences.zh: 賾答曰：「謹案：漢文帝已前，未有冠幘，即是文帝以來所制也。

translations.literal: Ze replied: "Respectfully investigating: before Emperor Wen of Han there were no cap-and-turban headdresses; this must be what was made from Emperor Wen's time onward."
translations.idiomatic: Ze replied: "Upon investigation, no caps with turbans appear before Emperor Wen of Han; this style must date from his reign onward."

sentences.zh: 臣見魏大司農盧元明撰《嵩高山廟記》云：『有神人，以玉為形，像長數寸，或出或隱，出則令世延長。

translations.literal: Your subject has seen Lu Yuanming of the Wei, Grand Minister of Agriculture, compose Mount Song Temple Record saying: 'There is a divine being shaped in jade, the image several inches long, sometimes appearing sometimes hidden; when it appears it makes the age extend long.'
translations.idiomatic: I have seen in the Mount Song Temple Record by Lu Yuanming, Grand Minister of Agriculture under Wei: 'A divine being shaped in jade, several inches tall, appears and vanishes; when it appears, the age is prolonged.'

sentences.zh: 』伏惟陛下，應天順人，定鼎嵩、雒，嶽神自見，臣敢稱慶。

translations.literal: Humbly considering Your Majesty: you responded to Heaven and followed the people, fixed the tripod at Song and Luo, the mountain deity has shown itself—your subject ventures to proclaim congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has answered Heaven and won the people's hearts, established the throne at Song and Luo—and now the mountain spirit has revealed itself. I venture to offer my congratulations.

sentences.zh: 」因再拜，百官畢賀。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bowed twice; all officials congratulated together.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed twice, and all the officials joined in congratulation.

sentences.zh: 天子大悅，賜縑二百匹。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was greatly pleased and bestowed two hundred bolts of fine silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and granted him two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 從駕往太山，詔問賾曰：「何處有羊腸阪？

translations.literal: Following the imperial procession to Mount Tai, an edict asked Ze: "Where is Sheep's Intestines Slope?"
translations.idiomatic: On the journey to Mount Tai, the emperor asked Ze: "Where is Sheep's Intestines Slope?"

sentences.zh: 」賾答曰：「臣案《漢書·地理志》，上党壺關縣有羊腸阪。

translations.literal: Ze replied: "Your subject investigates: In Book of Han, Treatise on Geography, Shangdang, Huguan county has Sheep's Intestines Slope."
translations.idiomatic: Ze replied: "According to the Treatise on Geography in the Book of Han, Huguan county in Shangdang has such a slope."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「不是。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "That is not it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That is not the one."

sentences.zh: 」又答曰：「臣案皇甫士安撰《地書》，云太原北九十里，有羊腸阪。

translations.literal: He again replied: "Your subject investigates Huangfu Shi'an's composition Book of the Earth, which says ninety li north of Taiyuan there is Sheep's Intestines Slope."
translations.idiomatic: Ze answered again: "In Huangfu Mi's Book of the Earth it says that ninety li north of Taiyuan there is a Sheep's Intestines Slope."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「是也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "That is it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That is the one."

sentences.zh: 」因謂牛弘曰：「崔祖浚所謂問一知二。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he said to Niu Hong: "Cui Zujun is what is called 'ask one and know two.'"
translations.idiomatic: He then said to Niu Hong: "Cui Zujun is the man of whom they say, 'ask one thing and he knows two.'"

sentences.zh: 五年，受詔與諸儒撰《區宇圖志》二百五十卷，奏之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he received an edict to compile with the Confucian scholars the Territorial Gazetteer in two hundred fifty rolls, and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was ordered to compile with the scholars the Territorial Gazetteer in two hundred fifty volumes and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝不善之，更令虞世基、許善心演為六百卷。

translations.literal: The emperor disliked it and instead ordered Yu Shiji and Xu Shansin to expand it into six hundred rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased with it and had Yu Shiji and Xu Shansin expand it to six hundred volumes.

sentences.zh: 以父憂去職，尋起令視事。

translations.literal: On his father's bereavement he left office; soon he was recalled and ordered to resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father but was soon recalled to resume his duties.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，授鷹揚長史。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign, he was appointed Chief Clerk of the Hawk-Flying Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign he was made Chief Clerk of the Hawk-Flying Army.

sentences.zh: 置遼東郡縣名，皆賾之議也。

translations.literal: The establishment of Liaodong commandery and county names—all were Ze's proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The names given to the commanderies and counties in Liaodong were all Ze's proposals.

sentences.zh: 奉詔作《東征記》。

translations.literal: By imperial order he composed Record of the Eastern Expedition.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he wrote the Record of the Eastern Expedition.

sentences.zh: 九年，除越王長史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was appointed Chief Clerk to the Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed Chief Clerk to the Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 于時山東盜賊蜂起，帝令撫慰高陽、襄國，歸首者八百餘人。

translations.literal: At that time bandits east of the mountains rose like bees; the emperor ordered him to pacify Gaoyang and Xiangguo; those who surrendered numbered more than eight hundred.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose throughout the eastern provinces, the emperor sent him to pacify Gaoyang and Xiangguo; more than eight hundred surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十二年，從駕江都。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he followed the imperial procession to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he accompanied the emperor to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及之弑帝也，引為著作郎，稱疾不起。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji murdered the emperor, he was summoned as Composition Draftsman but pleaded illness and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuwen Huaji murdered the emperor, Ze was offered the post of Composition Draftsman but pleaded illness and refused to serve.

sentences.zh: 在路發疾，卒于彭城，年六十九。

translations.literal: On the road he fell ill, and died at Pengcheng, age sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill on the road and died at Pengcheng at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 賾與河南元善、河東柳䛒、太原王劭、吳興姚察、琅琊諸葛潁、信都劉焯、河間劉炫相善，每因休假，清談竟日。

translations.literal: Ze was friendly with Yuan Shan of Henan, Liu Bian of Hedong, Wang Shao of Taiyuan, Yao Cha of Wuxing, Zhuge Ying of Langya, Liu Zhuo of Xindu, and Liu Xuan of Hejian; whenever on leave they would converse in pure talk throughout the day.
translations.idiomatic: Ze was close friends with Yuan Shan of Henan, Liu Bian of Hedong, Wang Shao of Taiyuan, Yao Cha of Wuxing, Zhuge Ying of Langye, Liu Zhuo of Xindu, and Liu Xuan of Hejian; on their days off they would talk together from morning till night.

sentences.zh: 所著詞、賦、碑、志十餘萬言，撰《洽聞志》七卷，《八代四科志》三十卷。

translations.literal: Compositions in lyrics, fu, stele, and chronicle exceeded one hundred thousand words; he compiled Comprehensive Accounts in seven rolls and Records of Eight Dynasties and Four Categories in thirty rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote more than one hundred thousand words in lyrics, rhapsodies, steles, and memorials, and compiled Comprehensive Accounts in seven volumes and Records of Eight Dynasties and Four Categories in thirty volumes.

sentences.zh: 未及施行，江都傾覆，咸為煨燼。

translations.literal: Before they could be put into practice, Jiangdu collapsed; all became glowing embers.
translations.idiomatic: Before any could be published, Jiangdu fell; all were burned to ash.

sentences.zh: 徐則，東海郯人也。

translations.literal: Xu Ze was a man of Tan in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ze came from Tan in Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 幼沈靜，寡嗜欲，受業于周弘正，善三玄，精於論議，聲擅都邑。

translations.literal: In youth deep and quiet, with few desires, he studied under Zhou Hongzheng, excelled in the Three Profundities, was skilled in disputation, and his fame dominated the capital districts.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was calm and reserved, with few desires; he studied under Zhou Hongzheng, mastered the Three Profundities, and excelled in debate; his renown filled the capital.

sentences.zh: 則歎曰：「名者實之賓，吾其為賓乎！

translations.literal: Ze sighed and said: "Name is the guest of reality—am I to be the guest!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ze sighed and said, "Fame is the guest of substance—am I to be the guest?

sentences.zh: 」遂懷棲隱之操，杖策入縉雲山。

translations.literal: Thereupon he cherished the resolve to dwell in reclusion, staff in hand entered Jinyun Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: With that he resolved to withdraw from the world and, staff in hand, made his way into Mount Jinyun."

sentences.zh: 後學者數百人苦請教授，則謝而遣之。

translations.literal: Later several hundred students earnestly begged him to teach; Ze declined and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Later hundreds of students begged him to teach, but he refused and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 不娶妻，常服巾褐。

translations.literal: He did not marry and regularly wore turban-cloth and coarse brown.
translations.idiomatic: He never married and always wore a scholar's cap and coarse hemp robes.

sentences.zh: 陳太建中，應召來憩於至真觀。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era of Chen, he responded to summons and came to rest at the Zhizhen Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chen Taijian era he answered a summons and stayed at the Abbey of Perfect Truth.

sentences.zh: 期月，又辭入天台山。

translations.literal: After a full month, he again took leave and entered Mount Tiantai.
translations.idiomatic: After a month he withdrew again into Mount Tiantai.

sentences.zh: 因絕粒養性，所資唯松水而已，雖隆冬冱寒，不服綿絮。

translations.literal: Thereupon he abstained from grain to nourish his nature; what he relied on was only pine and water; even in deep winter's bitter cold he did not wear cotton padding.
translations.idiomatic: He lived on pine nuts and spring water alone; even in the depths of winter he wore no quilted clothes.

sentences.zh: 太傅徐陵為之刊山立頌。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Xu Ling carved a mountain inscription and erected a eulogy for him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Xu Ling carved an inscription on the mountain and erected a eulogy in his honor.

sentences.zh: 初在縉雲山，太極真人徐君降之曰：「汝年出八十，當為王者師，然後得道也。

translations.literal: When he was first on Jinyun Mountain, the Grand Ultimate Perfected Lord Lord Xu descended to him saying: "When your years pass eighty, you shall become teacher to a king; only then will you attain the Way."
translations.idiomatic: While he was on Mount Jinyun, the Perfected Lord Xu of the Grand Ultimate appeared to him and said, "When you pass eighty, you shall become a king's teacher—only then will you attain the Way."

sentences.zh: 」晉王廣鎮揚州，聞其名，手書召之曰：「夫道得眾妙，法體自然，包涵二儀，混成萬物，人能弘道，道不虛行。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin Guang held garrison at Yangzhou, heard his name, and by hand wrote summoning him, saying: "The Way obtains the multitude of subtleties; Law embodies Nature; it embraces the Two Measures and blends to form the ten thousand things; man can amplify the Way—the Way does not travel in vain."
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guang, Prince of Jin, was stationed at Yangzhou and heard of him, he wrote a personal summons: "The Way gathers all mysteries; its law embodies nature itself, embracing heaven and earth and shaping the ten thousand things. A man can enlarge the Way—the Way does not walk in emptiness."

sentences.zh: 先生履德養空，宗玄齊物，深曉義理，頗味法門。

translations.literal: The gentleman treads virtue and nourishes emptiness, takes the Profound as his cult and equalizes things, deeply understands principles of meaning, and has tasted many gates of the Law.
translations.idiomatic: You tread the path of virtue and cultivate inner stillness; you hold to the profound and see all things as one; you understand principle deeply and have savored the teachings of the Law.

sentences.zh: 悅性沖玄，恬神虛白，餐松餌術，棲息煙霞。

translations.literal: Your nature delights in the unadorned profound; your spirit is tranquil in vacant whiteness; you dine on pine and ingest arts of longevity; you dwell and rest in mist and rosy clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Your nature delights in purity; your spirit rests in tranquil clarity; you nourish yourself on pines and live by immortal arts, dwelling at ease among mountain mists and rosy clouds.

sentences.zh: 望赤城而待風雲，遊玉堂而駕龍鳳。

translations.literal: Gazing at Red Wall [Mount Chicheng] you await wind and clouds; roaming the Jade Hall you drive dragon and phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: You gaze toward Mount Chicheng awaiting the wind and clouds of destiny; you wander the Jade Hall riding dragon and phoenix.

sentences.zh: 雖復藏名台嶽，猶且騰實江、淮。

translations.literal: Though again you hide your name on terrace-peaks, still your fruiting renown rises in Jiang and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Though you hide your name among sacred peaks, your fame still ripens across the Jiang and Huai.

sentences.zh: 藉甚嘉猷，有勞寤寐。

translations.literal: Your excellent plans are greatly relied upon; they weary [us in] waking and sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: Your wise counsel is greatly to be relied upon—it haunts our waking and our dreams.

sentences.zh: 欽承素道，久積虛襟，側席幽人，夢想岩穴。

translations.literal: We respectfully inherit the plain Way, long amassed in an empty bosom; with side-turned mat we [await] the secluded man, dreaming of cliff caves.
translations.idiomatic: I have long revered the pure Way and kept an open heart; with mat turned sidewise I await a recluse, dreaming of those who dwell in mountain caves.

sentences.zh: 霜風已冷，海氣將寒，偃息茂林，道體休悆。

translations.literal: Frost-wind is already cold, sea-breath will soon be chill—recline and rest in the thick grove; the Way-body is at ease and well.
translations.idiomatic: The frost wind has turned cold and the sea air will soon bite—rest at ease in the deep forest; let your Way-honed body find its peace.

sentences.zh: 昔商山四皓，輕舉漢庭；

translations.literal: Of old the four hoary worthies of Shang Mountain lightly entered the Han court;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Four Hoary Heads of Mount Shangshan lightly took their place at the Han court;

sentences.zh: 淮南八公，來儀籓邸。

translations.literal: The eight gentlemen of Huainan came in ritual to the feudal residence.
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Gentlemen of Huainan came in ceremony to a prince's domain.

sentences.zh: 古今雖異，山谷不殊。

translations.literal: Ancient and present though different, valley and mountain are not apart.
translations.idiomatic: Past and present may differ, but valley and peak call alike.

sentences.zh: 市朝之隱，前賢已說。

translations.literal: The recluse within market and court—former worthies have already spoken of it.
translations.idiomatic: The sage who hides within the bustle of court and market—former sages have already described him.

sentences.zh: 導凡述聖。

translations.literal: Guide the vulgar, expound the sage.
translations.idiomatic: To guide the common and expound the sage.

sentences.zh: 非先生而誰？

translations.literal: If not the gentleman, who?
translations.idiomatic: Who but you could do this?

sentences.zh: 故遣使人，往彼延請，想無勞東帛，賁然來思，不待蒲輪，去彼空穀。

translations.literal: Therefore I send envoys to go there and extend invitation—thinking it need not trouble bolts of eastern silk; you will come with radiant thought, not waiting for rush-wheeled carriage, leaving that empty valley.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I send messengers to invite you in person. I trust you need no silken gifts to come forth with shining grace, nor wait for a carriage with rush wheels to leave your empty vale.

sentences.zh: 希能屈己，佇望披云。

translations.literal: I hope you can bend yourself; I stand awaiting parting the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: I hope you will humble yourself—I stand waiting for you to part the clouds and appear.

sentences.zh: 」則謂門人曰：「吾今年八十一，王來召我，徐君之旨，信而不征。

translations.literal: " Ze said to his disciples: "This year I am eighty-one; the king has come to summon me—Lord Xu's directive: trustworthy yet not yet fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ze said to his disciples, "I am eighty-one this year. The prince has summoned me. Lord Xu's prophecy is true, though the summons is not yet fulfilled."

sentences.zh: 」於是遂詣揚州。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he proceeded to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: With that he went to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉王將請受道法，則辭以時日不便。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin was about to request receiving the Way's teachings; Ze declined on grounds that the day and time were not convenient.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin was about to request instruction in the Way, Ze declined on the grounds that the day was not auspicious.

sentences.zh: 其後夕中，命待者取香火，如平常朝禮之儀，至於五更而死。

translations.literal: That night afterward, he ordered attendants to fetch incense and fire, as in his ordinary morning-rite ceremony; by the fifth watch he was dead.
translations.idiomatic: That night he ordered his attendants to bring incense and perform his usual morning rites; by the fifth watch he was dead.

sentences.zh: 支體柔弱如生，停留數旬，顏色不變。

translations.literal: His limbs were soft as if alive; detained several tens of days, his complexion did not change.
translations.idiomatic: His body remained soft as if alive; for several weeks his complexion did not change.

sentences.zh: 晉王下書曰：「天台真隱東海徐先生，虛確居宗，沖玄成德，齊物處外，檢行安身。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin issued a document saying: "Tiantai's true recluse, Donghai's Lord Xu—void and assured, dwelling as cult-leader; unadorned profound forming virtue; equalizing things while standing apart, restraining conduct to settle body.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin issued a proclamation: "The true recluse of Tiantai, Lord Xu of Donghai—serene and steadfast as his faith, profound in virtue, treating all things as one while standing apart, governing his conduct to settle his soul.

sentences.zh: 草褐蒲衣，餐松餌朮，棲隱靈岳，五十餘年。

translations.literal: Grass-brown and rush-cloth robes, dining on pine and ingesting atractylodes, dwelling hidden on spirit peaks, more than fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: In hemp and rush-cloth robes he fed on pine nuts and atractylodes, dwelling on sacred peaks for more than fifty years.

sentences.zh: 卓矣仙才，飄然騰氣，千尋萬頃，莫測其涯。

translations.literal: Outstanding immortal talent, floating aloft in ascending qi—a thousand fathoms, ten thousand leagues, none can fathom his shore.
translations.idiomatic: A transcendent spirit, loftier than measure, rising on powers none can fathom.

sentences.zh: 寡人欽承道風，久餐德素，頻遣使乎，遠此延屈，冀得虔受上法，式建良緣。

translations.literal: I few-men respectfully inherit the Way's wind, long feasted on plain virtue, repeatedly sent envoys to extend his bending here, hoping to devoutly receive the upper Law and erect a good affinity.
translations.idiomatic: I have long revered your Way and savored your virtue, sending envoys again and again to bring you here, hoping to receive your highest teachings and forge a noble bond.

sentences.zh: 至止甫爾，未淹旬日，厭塵羽化，反真靈府。

translations.literal: Arriving and stopping but just then, not flooding ten days, weary of dust he feather-transformed, returned to true spirit-palace.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely arrived, less than ten days, when weary of the dusty world he ascended, returning to the realm of true spirits.

sentences.zh: 身體柔軟，顏色不變，經方所謂屍解地仙者哉。

translations.literal: Body soft, complexion unchanging—the classics' directions call this corpse-liberation earthly immortal, do they not?
translations.idiomatic: His body soft, his face unchanged—is this not what the scriptures call corpse liberation, an earthly immortal?

sentences.zh: 誠復師禮未申，而心許有在，雖忘怛化，猶愴於懷。

translations.literal: Truly, though master-rites were not displayed, yet heart-vows had standing; though forgetting to be anxious about transformation, still I am grief-stricken in the bosom.
translations.idiomatic: Though I never completed the rites of discipleship, my heart had already pledged itself; though I know he has passed beyond sorrow, grief yet fills my breast.

sentences.zh: 喪事所資，隨須供給。

translations.literal: What the funeral affairs require—supply as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Provide whatever his funeral requires.

sentences.zh: 霓裳羽蓋，既且騰雲；

translations.literal: Rainbow robes and feathered canopy—already he ascends the clouds;
translations.idiomatic: Clad in rainbow robes beneath a canopy of feathers, he has already risen on clouds;

sentences.zh: 空槨餘衣，詎藉墳壟？

translations.literal: Empty coffin, remaining clothes—how would they borrow from tomb-mound?
translations.idiomatic: What need has an empty coffin or leftover garments for an earthly mound?

sentences.zh: 但杖舄在爾，可同俗法。

translations.literal: Only staff and shoes are here—with these one may follow common custom.
translations.idiomatic: Only his staff and shoes remain—bury these according to common custom.

sentences.zh: 宜遣使人，送還天台定葬。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to send envoys to escort back to Tiantai for settled burial."
translations.idiomatic: Send envoys to escort his remains to Tiantai for burial there."

sentences.zh: 是時，自江都至天台，在道多見則徒步，云得放還。

translations.literal: At that time, from Jiangdu to Tiantai, on the road many saw Ze walking on foot, saying he had been released to return.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, along the road from Jiangdu to Tiantai, many reported seeing Xu Ze walking on foot, saying he had been freed to go home.

sentences.zh: 至其舊居，取經書道法，分遣弟子，仍令淨掃一房，曰：「若有客至，宜延之於此。

translations.literal: Reaching his old dwelling, he took scriptures and Way-methods, distributed to disciples, and still ordered clean sweeping of one room, saying: "If guests come, it is fitting to extend them here.
translations.idiomatic: He reached his old dwelling, gathered his scriptures and Daoist texts, distributed them among his disciples, and had a room swept clean, saying, "If guests should come, receive them here.

sentences.zh: 」然後跨石梁而去，不知所之。

translations.literal: " Then he crossed the stone bridge and departed—none knew where.
translations.idiomatic: Then he crossed the Stone Bridge and went away—none knew where.

sentences.zh: 須臾屍柩至，知其靈化，時年八十二。

translations.literal: In a moment the corpse-coffin arrived; they knew his spirit had transformed; his age at the time was eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Presently his coffin arrived, and they knew his spirit had transformed; he was eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 晉王聞而益異之，賵物千段，遣畫工圖其狀，令柳{巧言}為之贊。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin heard and was all the more astonished; funeral gifts a thousand lengths, sent painters to depict his appearance, ordered Liu Jian to compose praise for it.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin, hearing this, was all the more amazed; he sent a thousand lengths of funeral gifts, had painters depict Xu Ze's likeness, and commissioned Liu Jian to write an encomium.

sentences.zh: 時有建安宋玉泉、會稽孔道茂、丹陽王遠知等，亦行辟穀道，以松水自給，皆為煬帝所重。

translations.literal: At the time there were Jian'an's Song Yuquan, Kuaiji's Kong Daomao, Danyang's Wang Yuanzhi and others who also practiced grain-abstaining Way, supplying themselves with pine and water—all were heavily esteemed by Emperor Yang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Song Yuquan of Jian'an, Kong Daomao of Kuaiji, Wang Yuanzhi of Danyang, and others also practiced fasting from grain, living on pine nuts and spring water, and all were held in high regard by Emperor Yang.

sentences.zh: 張文詡

translations.literal: Zhang Wensu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wensu

sentences.zh: 張文詡，河東人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Wensu was a man of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wensu was from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父琚，開皇中，為洹水令，以清正聞。

translations.literal: His father Ju, in the Kaihuang era, was Magistrate of Huanshui, known for purity and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ju served as Magistrate of Huanshui during the Kaihuang era and was known for integrity.

sentences.zh: 文詡博覽群書，特精《三禮》。

translations.literal: Wensu broadly perused many books, especially expert in the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Wensu read widely and was especially masterful in the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝方引天下名儒碩學之士，文詡時游太學，博士房暉遠等莫不推伏之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui was just drawing the world's famous Confucians and great scholars; Wensu at the time roamed the Imperial Academy—Erudites Fang Xianyuan and others none did not bow in submission to him.
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Wen was gathering renowned scholars from across the realm, Wensu studied at the Imperial Academy, and erudites such as Fang Xianyuan all deferred to him.

sentences.zh: 書侍御史皇甫誕，一時朝彥，恆執弟子之禮，以所乘馬就學邀屈。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief of Writings Huangfu Dan, a court luminary of the time, constantly observed disciple's rites, with his ridden horse going to study to invite and bend him.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Dan, Censor-in-Chief, one of the leading men at court, always treated him as his teacher and came on horseback to invite him to lectures.

sentences.zh: 文詡遂每牽馬步進，意在不因人自致也。

translations.literal: Wensu thereupon each time led the horse and walked forward—his intent lay in not achieving himself through others.
translations.idiomatic: Wensu would walk alongside, leading the horse himself, unwilling to gain distinction through another man's patronage.

sentences.zh: 右僕射蘇威聞而召之，與語大悅，勸令從官，文詡固辭。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Su Wei heard and summoned him, conversed greatly delighted, urged him to take office—Wensu firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Wei, Vice Director of the Right, heard of him and summoned him, he found their conversation delightful and urged Wensu to enter government service, but Wensu firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 仁壽末，學廢，文詡策杖而歸，灌園為業。

translations.literal: At the end of Renshou, learning was abolished; Wensu staff in hand returned home, tending gardens as occupation.
translations.idiomatic: When the academy closed at the end of the Renshou era, Wensu took his staff and returned home to tend his garden.

sentences.zh: 州郡頻舉，皆不應命。

translations.literal: Provinces and commanderies repeatedly recommended him—all did not respond to summons.
translations.idiomatic: The provinces repeatedly recommended him, but he never answered their summons.

sentences.zh: 事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Serving his mother, he was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He was famed for filial devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 每以德化人，鄉黨頗移風俗。

translations.literal: Each time by virtue he transformed people; in village and hamlet customs were considerably shifted.
translations.idiomatic: He continually won people over through virtue, and his village gradually changed its ways.

sentences.zh: 嘗有人夜中竊刈其麥者，見而避之。

translations.literal: Once someone at night secretly reaped his wheat—he saw him and avoided him.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when someone stole into his fields at night to cut his wheat, Wensu saw him and stepped aside.

sentences.zh: 盜因感悟，棄麥而謝。

translations.literal: The thief thereby gained awakening, abandoned the wheat and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: The thief was moved to repentance, abandoned the wheat, and apologized.

sentences.zh: 文詡慰諭之，自誓不言，固令持去。

translations.literal: Wensu comforted and instructed him, swore himself not to speak, firmly ordered him to carry it away.
translations.idiomatic: Wensu comforted him, vowed never to speak of it, and insisted he take the wheat away.

sentences.zh: 經數年，盜者向鄉人說之，始為遠近所悉。

translations.literal: After several years, the thief told fellow villagers—only then was it known far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Only years later did the thief tell his neighbors, and then the story became known far and wide.

sentences.zh: 鄰家築牆，心有不直，文詡因毀舊堵以應之。

translations.literal: A neighbor's family built a wall; in heart [the line] was not straight—Wensu therefore destroyed the old barrier to match it.
translations.idiomatic: When a neighbor built a wall that encroached on his line, Wensu tore down his own old wall to align with it.

sentences.zh: 文詡常有腰疾，會醫者自言善禁，文詡令禁之，遂為刀所傷，至於頓伏床枕。

translations.literal: Wensu often had waist ailment; encountering a physician who declared himself good at taboo-healing, Wensu ordered him to perform taboo-healing—thereupon he was wounded by a knife, reaching to collapsing prostrate on bed-pillow.
translations.idiomatic: Wensu suffered from a chronic back ailment. A physician who claimed skill in spirit-healing was summoned; during the treatment Wensu was cut by a knife and collapsed upon his bed.

sentences.zh: 醫者叩頭請罪。

translations.literal: The physician knocked head asking forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: The physician kowtowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 文詡遽遣之，因為隱，謂妻子曰：「吾昨風眩，落坑所致。

translations.literal: Wensu hastily sent him off, and on his behalf concealed it, telling wife and children: "Yesterday I had wind-dizziness, caused by falling into a pit.
translations.idiomatic: Wensu hurried him away and concealed the matter, telling his wife, "I had a dizzy spell yesterday and fell into a ditch.

sentences.zh: 」其掩人短，皆此類也。

translations.literal: " His covering others' shortcomings—all were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his way of shielding others' faults.

sentences.zh: 州縣以其貧素，將加賑恤，輒辭不受。

translations.literal: Province and county because of his poverty and plainness were about to add relief—he repeatedly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When the local authorities wished to grant him relief because of his poverty, he always refused.

sentences.zh: 嘗閒居無事，從容歎曰：「老冉冉而將至，恐修名之不立！

translations.literal: Once at leisure with nothing to do, calmly sighing he said: "Old age slowly approaching will arrive—I fear a cultivated name not established!
translations.idiomatic: Once in quiet leisure he sighed and said, "Old age creeps upon me—I fear my good name may never be made!

sentences.zh: 」以如意擊幾自樂，皆有處所，時人方之閔子騫、原憲焉。

translations.literal: " With ruyi-scepter striking the armrest for self-enjoyment—all had its place; men of the time compared him to Min Ziqian and Yuan Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He would tap his armrest with a ruyi in quiet contentment, each gesture measured and sure; men of the day compared him to Min Ziqian and Yuan Xian.

sentences.zh: 終於家，鄉人為立碑頌，號曰張先生。

translations.literal: He ended at home; fellow villagers erected a stele-eulogy for him, styled Master Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home; his neighbors erected a memorial stele to praise him, addressing him as Master Zhang.

sentences.zh: 論曰：古之所謂隱逸者，非伏其身而不見也，非閉其言而不出也，非藏其智而不發也。

translations.literal: Discussion says: what ancients called secluded and retired is not hiding the body and not being seen, not closing speech and not issuing forth, not concealing wisdom and not issuing forth.
translations.idiomatic: The historians remark: what the ancients called a recluse was not one who hid his body from sight, sealed his lips, or buried his wisdom.

sentences.zh: 蓋以恬淡為心，不皦不昧，安時處順，與物無私者也。

translations.literal: Rather, taking plain calm as heart, neither bright nor dim, settling the age and placing oneself in accord, with things without selfishness—that is the kind.
translations.idiomatic: Rather, he keeps a tranquil heart, neither ostentatious nor obscure, rests in his time and accords with circumstance, and harbors no selfishness toward the world.

sentences.zh: 眭誇忘懷纓冕，畢志丘園，或隱不違親，貞不絕俗；

translations.literal: Sui Kua forgot crown and cap-sash, fulfilled will in hill-garden; some hide without violating kin, chaste without cutting off custom;
translations.idiomatic: Sui Kua forgot rank and office and found his fulfillment in gardens and hills; some hid without abandoning family duty, others kept faith without cutting themselves off from the world;

sentences.zh: 或不教而勸，虛往實歸，非有自然純德，其孰能至此？

translations.literal: Or without teaching yet moving, empty going yet solid returning—if one lacked inborn pure virtue, who could reach here?
translations.idiomatic: Or won men without preaching and sent them home enriched—who but a man of pure inborn virtue could achieve such ends?

sentences.zh: 然文詡見傷無慍，徐則志在沈冥，不可親疏，莫能貴賤，皆可謂抱樸之士矣。

translations.literal: Yet Wensu when wounded harbored no anger; Xu Ze's will lay in deep obscurity—no one could be intimate or distant, none could deem noble or base—all may be called gentlemen who embrace the unhewn.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wensu, injured yet without resentment, and Xu Ze, whose purpose lay in deepest obscurity, alike beyond favor or neglect, beyond high or low esteem—both may be called men who embrace simplicity.

sentences.zh: 崔廓感於屈辱，遂以肥遁見稱；

translations.literal: Cui Kuo moved by humiliation, thereby by "fat escape" was styled renowned;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Kuo, stung by humiliation, won fame as one who made a stately withdrawal;

sentences.zh: 祖浚文籍之美，足以克隆堂構。

translations.literal: Zujun's literary elegance was sufficient to continue the hall's framework.
translations.idiomatic: While his son Zujun's mastery of letters was enough to sustain the family's standing.

sentences.zh: 父子雖動靜殊方，其于成名一也，美哉！

translations.literal: Father and son though movement and stillness differed in direction, in achieving name it was one—how beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: Father and son took different paths, yet each won renown in his own way—how admirable!
